findings.evidence: Fine-tuning does not make the model smaller — pruning is a separate operation.
findings.issue: Terminology Precision. 'Pruning' usually refers to structural pruning or weight pruning. Distillation is another way to make a model smaller. This sentence is technically correct but might be read as a blanket statement against all model reduction techniques (e.g. quantization). Given Chapter 7 handles quantization extensively, it's fine.

findings.evidence: Output tokens per dollar (single-stream decode, 50 tok/s) 9,000 output tokens per dollar
findings.issue: Contextual Inconsistency. Section 5.3.2 uses 50 tok/s as an 'ILLUSTRATIVE' low-batch rate. However, the main table (4-2) and previous chapters established 40 tok/s (25ms/token) as the SLO target/canonical budget. Why switch to 50? The text says 'chosen to demonstrate the per-dollar method'. It also says '50 tok/s... faster than the canonical 40 tok/s... without contradicting it'. It is slightly confusing to use a non-canonical number for the 'Worked Example' of selection, as it deviates from the 'Canonical' theme of the book's running example. The note clarifies it is 'conservative against batched', but why not use the canonical 40? 40 * 3600 / 20 = 7200 tokens/dollar. The book uses 9000. This deviation makes cross-referencing difficult.
findings.fix_instruction: Consider using the canonical 40 tok/s to maintain consistency with the main scenario, or explicitly flag '50 tok/s' as a 'Best-case illustrative' distinct from the 'SLO-bound Canonical'.

findings.chapter: Ch. 5 — From Workload to Model Selection
findings.evidence: PDF p. 119: "At ~50 tok/s aggregate throughput, the effective cost is ~$0.40 per (tok/s) per hour"; later on the same page: "the ~50 tok/s used here is a deliberately low-batch (single-stream) generation rate — conservative against batched serving rates".
findings.issue: The same 50 tok/s quantity is first called 'aggregate throughput' and then clarified as a low-batch single-stream rate. 'Aggregate' misleadingly suggests batched or whole-fleet throughput, which is exactly the interpretation the following reconciliation note warns against.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace the first phrase with 'single-stream host generation rate' or 'single-stream 50 tok/s operating point', and reserve 'aggregate' for explicitly batched or fleet-wide token rates.
